value.body: Indian nurses work in the Gulf countries, the UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, Canada and the US, among others. Each country has its own licensing exam, English-language requirement and registration body. The process usually takes months and much of the cost is paid upfront.

items.label: UK licensing
items.note: Computer-based test (CBT) then a practical OSCE

items.label: Gulf licensing
items.value: Country or emirate health authority exam
items.note: For example DHA, DOH, MOH or the Saudi Commission

items.label: English test
items.note: Required score set by each regulator

value.title: How you get in
value.body: B.Sc Nursing (GNM is accepted in some countries) with State Nursing Council registration; many employers also ask for post-registration clinical experience. Pass the destination's English test and licensing exam, then apply for registration and a work visa — through an employer, a state-run overseas recruitment agency, or a recruiting agent registered on the MEA's eMigrate portal.

value.title: At a glance
items: Costs add up — exams, credential checks, language tests, visas and travel — and are often paid before a job is confirmed.
Recruitment fraud is a known risk; check that an agent is registered on eMigrate, and treat large upfront placement fees as a warning sign.
Gulf jobs rarely lead to permanent residence; the UK, Australia, Canada and the US can, under their own immigration rules.
Experience in ICU, theatre or emergency care is often asked for.
